Chapter 8: The Struggle Within—Healing the Wounds of Violence
The fight for freedom... it leaves scars, doesn’t it? Not just on bodies, but on families, and on the soul of an entire nation. The violence that once felt necessary for liberation doesn’t just disappear—it lingers, shaping how people connect with each other, and even how they see themselves. Now, the real challenge isn’t just about defeating an enemy on the outside. It’s about healing the wounds that are left behind.
Picture this: A former fighter, now a father, wakes up in the middle of the night, haunted by old dreams of battle. He desperately wants to create a better life for his children, but the habits of war... those are tough to shake. He finds himself quick to anger, always a bit suspicious, struggling to trust anyone—even the people closest to him. His wife worries, silently, that the violence of the past could poison their family’s future.
And stories like this? They’re everywhere. The trauma from conflict seeps into daily life, making it so hard to build the trust and cooperation that a healthy society needs. Old rivalries suddenly come back to life, fueled by memories of betrayal and loss. The urge to settle old scores, to seek revenge—it’s strong, and sometimes feels almost impossible to resist.
Most folks don’t realize just how deep these wounds actually go. The violence of colonialism wasn’t just about physical pain—it was psychological, emotional, cultural. It taught people to see themselves, and each other, as enemies. To believe that power only comes through force.
Healing from that? It’s slow. It’s uncertain. And it takes more than just new laws or fresh institutions. It asks for real honesty about what happened, space to grieve, the courage to forgive, and a commitment to building new ways of relating to each other. That’s why community gatherings, storytelling, and rituals of remembrance become so important—they help people make sense of the past, together.
But you know what? There’s hope, even in the smallest of moments. Maybe it’s a neighbor lending a hand to rebuild a damaged home, or a group of former rivals coming together for a community project. These little acts of kindness remind us that change is possible. The future doesn’t have to be trapped by the past.
So here’s the real takeaway: True liberation isn’t just about breaking chains. It’s about healing hearts. That work never really ends—and every single person has a part to play.
